structured_output.summary: One releasable change: opt-in detached upgraded streams in reverse_proxy, with stream logs, hijack-safety fixes in the response-writer chain, stream metrics, config/docs and tests. Docs are limited to the Caddyfile doc comment and JSON struct field comments, as the intents require.

intents.rationale: No stream_detached field exists; streams are always registered on the Handler and closed in Cleanup.
Detached streams need a process-global registry keyed by upstream so a reload closes only streams whose upstream is gone from the new config.
The default path must remain as it is; it needs regression coverage and must be kept intact while the detached path is added.
No stream_logs block exists; the handshake is not distinguished in logging.
Close is only logged at debug on the handler logger; it must go through the access logger with a configurable level.
The handler calls rw.WriteHeader then hijacks via the recording writer, whose Hijack wraps the conn in hijackedConn; post-hijack writes must be refused and bytes copied on the raw conn.
encode and intercept wrap the writer and must pass 101/hijacked responses through untouched; verify and fix.
The h2 extended CONNECT path uses h2ReadWriteCloser and must register and detach like hijacked conns; HTTP/1.1 detached must work too.
Only upstreams_healthy metric exists; add stream metrics.
Caddyfile parsing, doc comment and JSON struct fields must be added.
Add new integration tests with a real server and clients.
Add unit tests for registry, Caddyfile parsing, metrics, and writer hijack behaviour.

criteria.text: With stream_detached set (Caddyfile and JSON), an established WebSocket/Upgrade stream stays open and passes data after a config reload.
In detached mode, after a reload that removes an upstream, streams to that upstream are closed while streams to retained upstreams keep working.
Without stream_detached, upgraded streams are closed on reload, and with stream_close_delay they stay open until the delay elapses.
stream_logs { skip_handshake } suppresses the access log entry for the upgrade handshake; by default it is logged. Caddyfile parses to JSON correctly.
Stream close is logged via the access logger when logger_name access is configured, at a configurable level defaulting to DEBUG.
After hijack, writes and WriteHeader on the recording writer are no-ops or errors and do not reach the connection; 101 is final; the proxy copies on the raw conn, not the hijackedConn wrapper.
WebSocket upgrades work through encode and through intercept with handle_response in the same route, and with access logging.
HTTP/2 extended CONNECT websocket works end to end over h2, and HTTP/1.1 upgrades work in detached mode.
Metrics for active streams, closed streams by result, duration, and bytes to/from the backend are recorded, each stream exactly once, including on timeout, error and reload close.
stream_detached and stream_logs appear in JSON struct fields and Caddyfile parsing, with doc comments in caddyfile.go and reverseproxy.go.
Integration tests cover reload survival/closure in both modes, h2 extended CONNECT, encode and intercept upgrades, and detached streams with access logging.
Unit tests cover the detached registry, Caddyfile parsing of new options, metrics accounting, and post-hijack writer behaviour.

tasks.summary: Order: (1) add config fields and Caddyfile parsing plus docs; (2) add stream metrics and a stream-logs/access-logger path; (3) add a global detached-stream registry keyed by upstream, used in handleUpgradeResponse and Cleanup/reload logic, leaving the default path unchanged; (4) fix hijack safety in caddyhttp responseRecorder/encode/intercept (no writes after hijack, copy on raw conn); (5) write unit then integration tests, updating existing streaming tests and adapt fixtures if they break.
